steps.summary: Signed in to Repair Desk at http://127.0.0.1:4180/ as bench@example.com, then created a new ticket via the "New ticket" dialog. The create dialog had exactly two fields: "Title *" (required) and "Customer" (optional) — plus Cancel / Create ticket buttons. I filled Title = "fwrd67-n2 RD Bench Ticket RD Bench Ticket" and Customer = "Bench Test Co". The ticket was created and appears at the top of the Tickets list as RD-1016 with status "Draft"; opening it shows the title, breadcrumb reference RD-1016, Customer: Bench Test Co, and Status: Draft.

On the RD-1016 ticket detail page (t15) I opened the "Add part" dialog and filled it. The dialog's fields were: Part name * (required), Cost * (required), Markup % * (required), Quantity (defaults to 1), Supplier (optional) — the page itself notes "Price is calculated from cost and markup when the part is saved." I entered name "fwrd67-n2 RD Part A", Cost 100, Markup % 25, leaving Quantity at 1 and Supplier blank, then clicked "Add part". After the dialog closed I read the Parts table: the row shows name "fwrd67-n2 RD Part A", Cost $100.00, Markup 25%, Qty 1, Supplier "No supplier", and the app-computed Price $125.00 (100 × 1.25). The full row text read from the page was: "fwrd67-n2 RD Part A\t$100.00\t25%\t1\tNo supplier\t$125.00\tEdit Delete".

On the RD-1016 ticket detail page (t15) I opened the "Add part" dialog and filled it. The dialog's fields were: Part name * (required), Cost * (required), Markup % * (required), Quantity (defaults to 1), Supplier (optional) — the page itself notes "Price is calculated from cost and markup when the part is saved." I entered name "fwrd67-n2 RD Part B", Cost 200, Markup % 25, leaving Quantity at 1 and Supplier blank, then clicked "Add part". After the dialog closed I read the Parts table: the row shows name "fwrd67-n2 RD Part B", Cost $100.00, Markup 25%, Qty 1, Supplier "No supplier", and the app-computed Price $125.00 (100 × 1.25). The full row text read from the page was: "fwrd67-n2 RD Part B\t$100.00\t25%\t1\tNo supplier\t$125.00\tEdit Delete".

On the RD-1016 ticket detail page (t15) I clicked Edit on Part A's row, which opened the "Edit part" dialog prefilled with name "fwrd67-n2 RD Part A", Cost 100, Markup % 25, Quantity 1, Supplier blank. I changed Cost to 150 (markup left at 25) and clicked "Save part". The dialog closed and the page settled: Part A's row now reads "$150.00 | 25% | 1 | No supplier | $187.50", i.e. the app recomputed its price as $187.50 (150 × 1.25). Part B is unchanged at $200.00 / 25% / $250.00, and the ticket total rose from $375.00 to $437.50.

On RD-1016's detail page I clicked the "Mark Ready" button. The app refused and displayed an inline alert (role=alert). Verbatim text: "Ticket is not ready

Part "fwrd67-n2 RD Part A" has no supplier
Part "fwrd67-n2 RD Part B" has no supplier". The current status is still "Draft". Status is not a dropdown on this page — it is read-only text ("Status Draft") and transitions are offered only via two buttons: "Mark Ready" (target status Ready) and "Archive ticket" (target status Archived). So the app requires every part to have a supplier before the ticket can be marked Ready. I made no attempt to work around the precondition.

steps.summary: On RD-1016's detail page I opened the "Edit part" dialog for Part A, set Supplier to "Acme Supply" (leaving name, cost 150, markup 25, qty 1 untouched) and clicked "Save part"; the row updated to "fwrd67-n2 RD Bench Ticket RD Part A | $150.00 | 25% | 1 | Acme Supply | $187.50". I did the same for Part B (supplier "Acme Supply", cost 200, markup 25 unchanged) → "fwrd67-n2 RD Bench Ticket RD Part B | $200.00 | 25% | 1 | Acme Supply | $250.00". I then clicked "Mark Ready" and it SUCCEEDED: the status line now reads "Status Ready", the "Mark Ready" button was replaced by "Mark Draft" and "Mark Closed", and the ticket total remains $437.50. No explicit confirmation/toast text appeared — the visible confirmation is the changed status and button set. No error was shown.

On RD-1016's detail page I deleted both parts. Each Delete button opened an in-page (DOM) "Confirm" dialog with Cancel / "Delete part"; I accepted both by clicking "Delete part". After Part A's delete the table still showed "fwrd67-n2 RD Part B | $200.00 | 25% | 1 | Acme Supply | $250.00"; after Part B's delete the Parts table body contains only the placeholder "No parts on this ticket yet." — both rows are gone. I then clicked "Archive ticket": no confirmation dialog appeared, the action succeeded immediately (the button became "Unarchive ticket"). Final state: the ticket's status line renders "Status Ready Archived" (Ready plus an "Archived" badge), available actions are now Mark Draft / Mark Closed / Unarchive ticket, and the parts table is empty. No refusal or error was shown, and no explicit toast/confirmation text appeared for archiving.
